provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Portrait of a friend
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify facial features.
The pupils should be able to draw a friend's portrait.
Introduction:
We have drawn shapes before. Today we draw our friends.
Content:
Look at your friend's face. Eyes, nose, mouth and hair. Draw what you see. Add their smile. Use crayons to color.
Class activity:
Each pupil chooses a friend to draw. They will sit and look at each other while drawing.
Evaluation questions:
What do we draw first on a face? What color is your friend's hair? How many eyes does a friend have?
Summary:
We can draw our friends by looking at their faces.

topics.title: Still life fruit bowl
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify fruits in a bowl.
The pupils should be able to draw still life objects.
Introduction:
We have drawn people before. Today we draw fruits on a table.
Content:
Look at the fruits in the bowl. Banana, orange, apple. Draw the shapes. Color what you see. Red apple, yellow banana.
Class activity:
Place fruits in a bowl in the middle of the class. Pupils take turns to draw the fruits.
Evaluation questions:
What fruits are in the bowl? What color is the banana? How many fruits did you draw?
Summary:
We can draw fruits we see in a bowl.

topics.title: Landscape
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify landscape elements.
The pupils should be able to create a layered picture.
Introduction:
We have drawn people and fruits. Today we draw outside scenes.
Content:
Sky is blue. Sun is yellow. Trees are green. House is brown. Draw sky first. Then sun, trees and house. Layer your picture.
Class activity:
Pupils draw a landscape with sky, sun, trees and house. They use different colors for each layer.
Evaluation questions:
What color is the sky? What comes first in a landscape? What is on top of the house?
Summary:
We can make beautiful landscapes with layers.

topics.title: Weaving progress
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to weave a simple mat.
The pupils should be able to create a two-color pattern.
Introduction:
We have drawn pictures. Today we weave like our grandparents.
Content:
Take two colors of paper. Cut into strips. Weave over and under. Make a pattern. Use red and blue.
Class activity:
Each pupil weaves a small mat using two colors of paper strips. They will show their patterns.
Evaluation questions:
What colors do you use? What comes first in weaving? How do you make a pattern?
Summary:
We can weave mats with beautiful patterns.

topics.title: Beads and buttons art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sort beads and buttons.
The pupils should be able to thread beads and glue buttons.
Introduction:
We have used paper and crayons. Today we use beads and buttons.
Content:
Sort beads by color. Thread beads on string. Glue buttons on paper. Make a class button tree.
Class activity:
Pupils sort beads and buttons. They thread beads to make necklaces. They glue buttons to make a big tree on chart paper.
Evaluation questions:
What colors are your beads? How do you thread beads? What can you make with buttons?
Summary:
We can make art with beads and buttons.

topics.title: Papier mache bowl
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to layer paper strips with paste.
The pupils should be able to paint a papier mache bowl.
Introduction:
We have made art with paper. Today we make a bowl with paper.
Content:\Tear paper into strips. Mix flour and water to make paste. Dip paper in paste. Layer on bowl shape. Let it dry. Paint your bowl.
Class activity:
Pupils tear paper strips, make paste, and layer it on a bowl shape. They paint their bowls when dry.
Evaluation questions:
What do we mix for paste? How do we layer paper? What color is your bowl?
Summary:
We can make bowls from paper and paste.

topics.title: Clay coil pots
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to roll clay coils.
The pupils should be able to stack and smooth clay coils.
Introduction:
We have made art with paper. Today we use clay to make pots.
Content:
Roll clay into long coils. Stack coils to make a pot. Smooth the coils with water. Paint your pot when dry.
Class activity:
Pupils roll clay into coils and stack them to make small pots. They smooth the coils and paint them.
Evaluation questions:
How do you roll clay? How do you stack coils? What color is your pot?
Summary:
We can make pots by rolling and stacking clay.

topics.title: Print making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to carve simple shapes on sponges.
The pupils should be able to repeat patterns in print making.
Introduction:
We have drawn and painted. Today we make prints with sponges.
Content:
Carve shapes on sponges. Dip in paint. Press on paper. Make patterns. Repeat your design.
Class activity:
Pupils carve simple shapes on sponges. They dip in paint and press on paper to make patterns.
Evaluation questions:
What shapes did you carve? How do you make prints? What patterns did you make?
Summary:
We can make beautiful prints with sponges.

topics.title: Cultural craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to decorate a calabash.
The pupils should be able to draw Adire patterns.
Introduction:
We have made many art works. Today we make Nigerian cultural art.
Content:
Decorate calabash with beads and paint. Draw Adire patterns with blue dye. Use traditional designs.
Class activity:
Pupils decorate small calabash shells and draw Adire patterns on paper using blue crayons.
Evaluation questions:
What is Adire art? How do you decorate calabash? What patterns did you draw?
Summary:
We can make Nigerian cultural crafts.

topics.title: Art festival
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to select their best artworks.
The pupils should be able to talk about their art work.
Introduction:
We have made many beautiful things. Today we show our best works.
Content:
Choose your three best works. Display them for everyone to see. Talk about what you made and why you like it.
Class activity:
Pupils display their best three artworks. They take turns to talk about their art work to the class.
Evaluation questions:
Which is your best work? Why do you like it? What did you learn in art class?
Summary:
We can share our art and talk about it.
